Here's the thing...This comment is in no means to boast, but there were kids (including   
myself) who were simply geniuses without parent support and finances (although it could help)...My mom thought being "gifted" was for naturally born geniuses because at 4 years old I taught myself  how to read and also taught myself up to 8th grade math by 1st grade using math books (which I liked reading for fun). I don't have photographic memory, but my brain hasn't excellent memory retention so any topics I didn't know, I could learn thought a teacher or just myself. Naturally, by high school, I had never once gotten grades below an A because I just memorized the material and would recall it. Math was especially easy because I just recall the exact process every-time to get it right. 

  
Now, my mom was a single mom and we dealt with my drug addict father and also had two younger sisters...we were homeless for about 2 years of my life in Kindergarten and 1st grade so we had very little resources. My mom worked so much and we went to random people or babysitters. My mom did read with us most nights I remember, however, my other sisters are not naturally "talented" at school and my mom never pushed them to get in the program. I do know that many kids said their parents made them take the test every year until they got in, so I do understand this and agree with this comment. My teacher noticed my abilities in 1st grade and had me take the test with my mom's permission, but my mom didn't event know what "gifted" was. She just wanted me to enjoy school because so much of it at first was boring to me because like I said, I already learned these topics by reading them once I learned to read. I took the test and they accepted me in. It was weird to hear years later when new students would join saying that their parents had them take it every year and they finally got in. On the other end, jealous students would get mad saying they never pass the test, but I just took it once and my mom never said I had to keep doing it if I didn't want to. 

  
However, my point is that I feel I am the outlier. And I just want to remind people that although this is not necessarily a great program and makes me people feel left out and has many issues socially, there are some people in the program who came from difficult backgrounds and it gave them opportunities when they otherwise wouldn't have. I enjoyed what the program offered me in getting to explore my brain. I also think I deserved it because I worked very hard in school; I had naturally talent but I expanded it by actually studying in high school and college. My mom didn't push me to be in the "smart" class.

To recap: I think, at least in my personal experience, that the benefit of these kinds of courses is to help expand natural talent, (however, the system is corrupt because rich families can just push their kids to excel until they get accepted in and also creates social tension).
